methods.label: m1

p1.role: upper bound of the federal funds target range after the September 2026 FOMC meeting, in percent per annum

a1.role: probability of a 25bp hike at the October 2026 FOMC meeting, as a fraction

a2.role: probability of no change at the October 2026 FOMC meeting, as a fraction

methods.rationale: Expected upper bound of the target range after the October 2026 FOMC meeting, using the CME FedWatch-implied probabilities of a hike (to 4.25%) versus a hold (at 4.00%). The formula is a probability-weighted average of the two possible outcomes, anchored on the observed current upper bound p1. Shared dependency: both probabilities come from the same market-implied distribution, so they are not ind
methods.error: formula_mc needs at least one input that is a quantity (not a share, ratio or %); a product of ratios cannot produce the target

kept.name: Probability of a 25bp hike at the October 2026 FOMC meeting
kept.rationale: CME FedWatch probabilities p42/p43 and p16/p17 put the hike probability at roughly 43-44% as of 2026-10-14. The range reflects uncertainty about how the market distribution evolves before the meeting and possible shifts after the September CPI release.
kept.applies_when: The next FOMC meeting after 2026-10-15 is the October 2026 meeting and market-implied probabilities remain the best available predictor of the decision.
kept.falsified_by: A subsequent CME FedWatch reading showing a materially different hike probability, or an FOMC statement/communication that clearly signals a different action.

kept.name: Probability of no change at the October 2026 FOMC meeting
kept.rationale: CME FedWatch probabilities p42/p43 and p16/p17 put the hold probability at roughly 56% as of 2026-10-14. The range reflects uncertainty about the market distribution before the meeting.
kept.applies_when: The next FOMC meeting after 2026-10-15 is the October 2026 meeting and market-implied probabilities remain the best available predictor of the decision.
kept.falsified_by: A subsequent CME FedWatch reading showing a materially different hold probability, or an FOMC statement/communication that clearly signals a different action.

directions.hypothesis: The current upper bound and recent changes provide a baseline; the next decision is likely a continuation or a modest adjustment. Historical patterns of rate changes around similar economic conditions can inform the likely direction.
directions.data_to_find: Current federal funds target range upper bound as of 2026-10-15; FOMC meeting dates for 2026; recent FOMC statements and minutes from 2026 meetings; historical frequency of rate changes at consecutive meetings.

directions.hypothesis: Fed funds futures and options prices embed market expectations for the target rate after the next FOMC meeting. The implied probability of various outcomes can directly constrain the upper bound.
directions.data_to_find: CME FedWatch tool probabilities for the next FOMC meeting as of 2026-10-15; fed funds futures prices for contract months covering the next meeting; OIS forward curve.

directions.hypothesis: Inflation, employment, and growth data influence FOMC decisions. Recent trends in CPI, PCE, unemployment, and GDP growth can signal whether the Fed is likely to hike, cut, or hold.
directions.data_to_find: Latest CPI, PCE, unemployment rate, nonfarm payrolls, and GDP growth data available before 2026-10-15; Fed's dual mandate progress; summary of economic projections (SEP) from recent meetings.

directions.hypothesis: The FOMC calendar and official statements provide the exact meeting date and any forward guidance. The Fed's dot plot and statement language can signal the likely policy action.
directions.data_to_find: Official FOMC meeting calendar for 2026 from the Federal Reserve website; latest FOMC statement and minutes; dot plot from the most recent SEP.

directions.hypothesis: Expert commentary and news articles often reflect consensus expectations for the next FOMC decision. The tone and content can indicate whether a change is anticipated.
directions.data_to_find: Recent articles from major financial news outlets (Reuters, Bloomberg, WSJ) discussing the next FOMC meeting; analyst forecasts; Fed speaker comments.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
